tier_reason: The README, doc/ (QUALITY_&_SPEED_FEATURES.md is a feature checklist only), CHANGELOG and releases give no speed number against libaom, and benches/ holds only internal kernel microbenchmarks. The numbers that do exist do not support a like-for-like win: the maintainers' issue #2759 says rav1e is slower than aomenc at matched presets, and an independent Av1an-based comparison shows rav1e is faster only at much worse BD-rate. So the claim stays directional, and the evidence against it is stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README only: 'The fastest and safest AV1 encoder' and 'most suitable for cases where libaom (the reference encoder) is too slow'. No number in the README, doc/, CHANGELOG or releases. The available numbers contradict a like-for-like win. rav1e issue #2759 (maintainer shssoichiro, 2021-07-09): 'our speed 6 still trails aomenc's cpu-used 6 by about 30% BD-rate, while also being slower (assuming one tile and no parallel encoding)', and speed 0 comes closer 'at the cost of rav1e being 2700% slower'. In the independent master-of-zen/AV1-benchmarks 2020.08.05 run (dota2 clip, 8-bit, Av1an chunked encoding), aomenc cpu-used 6 against rav1e speed 0 gives VMAF BD-rate -1.571% with 87.311% less time. rav1e speed 6 ran about 1.7x faster than aomenc cpu-used 6 (mean 38.9 s vs 66.9 s) at about 16% higher VMAF BD-rate, and speed 10 ran about 3.0x faster at about 63% higher BD-rate (derived from page data). Its speed advantage is therefore lower-quality output, which is different work.
corrections.caveats: No speed number against libaom in the repo. Counter-evidence: (1) rav1e issue #2759 (2021) says that at speed 6 rav1e trails aomenc cpu-used 6 by about 30% BD-rate and is also slower single-tile, and that speed 0 is 2700% slower; doc/QUALITY_&_SPEED_FEATURES.md lists frame-parallel encoding as missing in rav1e but present in libaom. (2) In master-of-zen/AV1-benchmarks (2020.08.05 and 2020.05.06 folders; public Av1an scripts and raw data files), rav1e's faster presets beat aomenc wall time only at clearly worse compression; at equal quality aomenc cpu-used 6 is about 7.9x faster than rav1e speed 0 (derived from page data). That benchmark is from 2020 and names no CPU model (one folder says a 12-thread system), no build flags and only 'git' snapshots of each encoder. Since then libaom has added faster presets and rav1e has had little speed work, and SVT-AV1 is widely reported as faster than both. The 'fastest' claim is therefore unsupported. The README's only measured number is an internal 11-13% gain from building with target-cpu=native or x86-64-v3. The crate is Rust with large hand-written assembly; it provides a C API (library, header, pkg-config) via cargo-c, so it can be called from C/C++. Licensed BSD-2-Clause plus the Alliance for Open Media Patent License 1.0.

notes: Kept as a notable (4.2k stars), active, BSD-2-Clause AV1 encoder with a C API, but its speed claim against libaom is contradicted by the project's own issue #2759 and by independent 2020 Av1an runs; the documented shortcoming is 'not faster than libaom at equal quality'. Metadata checked on the github.com repo and commits pages: BSD-2-Clause, 4.2k stars, 293 forks, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2026-08-31 ('Update to rand v0.10').
